Fix.description:
A replacement for a byte range of the file the finding is in.

Byte offsets rather than lines, because a fix is applied to text and re-linted afterwards; a
line-based patch has to be re-resolved after the fix above it lands, and that is where an
autofixer starts corrupting files.

description.description: One sentence, in the author's terms, on what changed.

end.description: Byte offset into the file's text, exclusive.

start.description: Byte offset into the file's text, inclusive.

Location.description:
Where a finding is, in the file a reader would open.

Lines and columns are 1-based, as every editor and every compiler reports them. `end` is
exclusive and optional: a rule that knows only the line says only the line rather than
inventing a span that would underline the wrong words.

advice.description: What to do about it. Static text per rule, so it costs nothing to produce.

confidence.description: The model's own estimate, for a finding a model wrote. Always 1.0 for anything computed.

file.description: The document this is about, relative to where slint was run.

message.description: One line, in the imperative or the indicative — never a scolding.

rule.description: The rule that fired, as it is written in a config file.

Reference.description:
Where a rule's claim comes from.

Not optional, and that is the point: every rule here asserts something about someone else's
writing, and an assertion with no source has to be taken on trust. A rule without a citation
does not get into the registry.

Report.description: Every skill looked at in one run.

fixed.description: Fixes written to disk during this run, when `--fix` was given.

notes.description:
About the run as a whole rather than one skill: arguments that were skipped, a discovery
that came up empty. Said out loud rather than inferred from an empty result.

Severity.description: How much a finding matters. Ordered worst-first, so a sort is a sort.

oneOf.description: The skill is broken, or the specification would refuse it.
It will work and behave worse than it should.
A judgement call worth seeing once.

SkillReport.description: Everything found in one skill, plus what could not be looked at.

notes.description:
Said out loud rather than inferred from an empty result — a pass that did not run, a file
that could not be read.

path.description: The skill's directory, relative to the run.

Source.description: What produced a finding, which is also how much it can be trusted.

oneOf.description: Read from the text. Exact, free, and always available.
Written by a language model. A reading, not a measurement.
Produced by a plugin, which may be either.

description: What `slint --format json` prints: an envelope whose `schemaVersion` says which shape follows, so a consumer can refuse one it was not written for. Data is on stdout and everything else on stderr, so piping is safe.

ok.description:
False when the run failed: anything at error severity was found, or `--max-warnings` was
exceeded. Warnings alone do not flip it — they are the linter's opinion, and a caller that
wants them fatal says so with --max-warnings, which this flag honours.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this shape. Pinned in `SCHEMA_VERSION`.
